### Sleep-Nutrition Interactions
**ID:** C62 **Created:** 2025-06-05

Sleep-nutrition interactions examine the bidirectional relationship between dietary choices and sleep quality, recognizing that both nutrition timing and composition significantly impact sleep patterns while sleep quality affects metabolic function and nutritional needs. This integrated approach optimizes both sleep and nutrition for enhanced recovery and performance.

**Core Components:**
- **Circadian Rhythm Optimization:** Nutritional strategies to support natural sleep-wake cycles through meal timing and specific nutrients, building on [[F1. Sleep Quality and Quantity]] and [[C3. Nutrient Timing]]
- **Sleep-Promoting Nutrients:** Strategic use of tryptophan, magnesium, melatonin precursors, and other compounds to enhance sleep quality, connected to [[A4. Micronutrients]] and [[C29. Nutrition for Recovery]]
- **Pre-Sleep Nutrition Protocols:** Evidence-based guidelines for evening nutrition that supports sleep onset and quality without disrupting metabolism, linking to [[C5. Pre, During, and Post-Exercise Nutrition]] and [[A8. Cardiovascular Physiology Fundamentals]]
- **Sleep Deprivation Nutritional Countermeasures:** Nutritional strategies to mitigate the negative effects of poor sleep on metabolism and performance, incorporating [[M2. Overtraining and Functional Overreaching]] and [[I1. Training and Hormonal Responses]]
- **Recovery Integration:** Understanding how sleep and nutrition work synergistically to optimize training adaptations and tissue repair, connected to [[M1. Recovery Modalities Evidence and Application]] and [[A36. Structural Adaptations to Training]]
